# Main-port tracking for fork PR #1109

This draft retains the complete fix from [#1109](https://github.com/AndreKurait/floci/pull/1109), including the public-reply work consolidated from [#1110](https://github.com/AndreKurait/floci/pull/1110). It is a pending port, not an applied or qualified implementation on main. Keep this review open and unmerged until the prerequisite APIs have been reconciled and the original regressions pass on main.

Native EC2 public-address traffic could reach a private listener but lose its reply in the VPC route filter. A stopped caller whose public interface disappeared could also quarantine surviving callers during route reconciliation. The original fix retains the native public interface, compiles destination-specific DNAT admission and reply rules from the subnet's longest-prefix route decisions, and withdraws only Docker-confirmed stopped or absent namespaces. Security groups, route withdrawal, more-specific denial, live invalid-interface failures, and cleanup ownership remain enforced.

## Prerequisites and existing reviews

Main at `d606843c4995b170536b84c3595a8ff6fc62f41b` uses `io.floci.aws` and has `VpcNetworkManager`, but lacks `VpcRoutingManager`, `VpcRoutingCommands`, the native public-peer route compiler, and the corresponding retirement APIs. A package rename alone cannot apply this fix.

| Existing main review | Retained branch | Required behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [#1035](https://github.com/AndreKurait/floci/pull/1035) | `tracking/pr-959-main-20261115` | Public frontend admission bound to ownership, security groups, and effective return routes. |
| [#1026](https://github.com/AndreKurait/floci/pull/1026) | `tracking/pr-1019-main-20261115` | Native public/API interfaces and source-preserving destination translation. |
| [#1037](https://github.com/AndreKurait/floci/pull/1037) | `tracking/native-peer-routing-restart-fences-main-20261115` | Native peer route ownership, dependency refresh, and restart/retirement fencing. |
| [#1042](https://github.com/AndreKurait/floci/pull/1042) | `tracking/open-dev-integration-main-20261115` | The reconciled native prerequisite stack and owner-safe helper retirement. |
| [#1091](https://github.com/AndreKurait/floci/pull/1091) | `track/main-vpc-routing-batches-20261116` | Bounded route-policy batches that drain writers before failure or retirement. |
| [#1092](https://github.com/AndreKurait/floci/pull/1092) | `track/main-helper-inspection-20261116` | Bounded helper inspection preserving stopped-caller ownership and failure handling. |

These are pending main reviews, not claims that those prerequisites already run on main. Reuse their reconciled implementations rather than replaying overlapping histories. The exact original combined prerequisite state for this patch remains the own-delta base above.

## Validation and remaining work

The original dev revision passed 117 selected tests, including three real EC2 packet cases and eight redirect cases, plus Maven packaging, Checkstyle, and repository gates. Its merged source passed the ordinary hosted checks and published the successful dev image. Those results qualify the dev source, not this pending main port.

This tracking revision verifies all seven retained paths, patch integrity, and exact tree reconstruction from the original base. It changes no executable main code. Before marking it ready:

1. Reconcile the prerequisite APIs with current main and replace the tracking artifacts with the focused implementation.
2. Retain the full original regression set, including external-client identity, security-group revoke/restore, internet-route revoke/restore, more-specific denials, stopped versus live-invalid interfaces, simultaneous retirement, and repeated Docker inspection failures.
3. Run the affected complete test classes, real EC2 packet cases, Maven packaging, Checkstyle, and repository gates on that main composition.
4. Keep dev evidence, main qualification, and downstream native fleet qualification separate.
